title: Kummer class of a divisor and its $c_1$
statement:
Fix the finite-coefficient setting of [def-pur-conventions], with $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ and arbitrary $n\geq1$. In the separated finite-type $k$-scheme setting of [sk-def-purity-conv], let $T\to B$ be smooth of relative dimension $d$ and let $D\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed subfamily smooth over $B$, of pure codimension one as in [def-pur-frame-class]. Thus $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. There is a canonical Kummer divisor class
$$\operatorname{cl}(D)\in H^2_D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A(1))$$
with supported cohomology as in [def-pur-support-cohomology] and twist as in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. It is the global class constructed from the line bundle $\mathcal O_T(D)$ with its canonical section trivializing it on $T\setminus D$, by the relative torsor Kummer connecting map [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology], followed by the coefficient map on roots prescribed in [def-pur-frame-class]. For every etale neighbourhood $U\to T$ on which $D_U$ has equation $f$, its restriction is
$$\operatorname{cl}(D)|_U=\partial\kappa(f)\in H^2_{D_U}(U,A(1)).$$
In particular it agrees with the rank-one frame class of [def-pur-frame-class], independently of the equation as in [lem-pur-frame-independence].

The same relative construction defines $\operatorname{cl}(E)$ for any effective Cartier divisor $E$ on $T$, including a sum of smooth divisors. If $D_1,D_2$ are such divisors and $Z=|D_1|\cup|D_2|$, then, after the canonical enlargement-of-support maps,
$$\operatorname{cl}(D_1+D_2)=\operatorname{cl}(D_1)+\operatorname{cl}(D_2)\quad\text{in }H^2_Z(T,A(1)).$$
Here $D_1+D_2$ is defined by the product of the two Cartier ideals, so locally its equation is $f_1f_2$, not the two-element frame $(f_1,f_2)$. Forgetting support sends $\operatorname{cl}(D)$ to $c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))\in H^2(T,A(1))$. Precisely, $c_1(L)$ means the ordinary etale Kummer connecting image of the frame-torsor class of $L$ [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor], at exponent $m=\ell^n$ killing $A$, mapped to the pro-etale twist by the same coefficient morphism as [def-pur-frame-class]. No $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$-module structure on $\mathbf G_m$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates] to $D\hookrightarrow T$ over $B$. The ambient finite-type setting is explicitly that of [sk-def-purity-conv]. Thus $T$ and $D$ are finite type over $k$, hence locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field has just the two ideals $0,k$, so its spectrum is Noetherian). At a point $y\in D$, the coordinate chart gives a regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_b$ in $R=\mathcal O_{T,y}$ defining $\mathcal O_{D,y}$. Each $f_j$ lies in the maximal ideal of its successive quotient and is a nonzerodivisor there. The successive quotients remain Noetherian, since their ideals correspond to ideals of $R$ containing the quotient ideal, and the images of generators generate. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] successively to obtain $\dim R=\dim\mathcal O_{D,y}+b$. The pure-codimension convention in [def-pur-frame-class] says the difference is one, so $b=1$. Thus locally $\mathcal I_D=(f)$ with $f$ a nonzerodivisor; off $D$ the ideal is the unit ideal. This proves that $D$ is Cartier and that one-function frames exist, without presuming regularity of the base. We will construct the global class rather than infer a global cohomology class from equality of local classes.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, lemma-etale-local-structure, applied to the first sentence of the blueprint proof

proof.text: For any effective Cartier divisor $E$ put $L_E=\mathcal I_E^\vee$ as in [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. On a chart $\mathcal I_E=(f_a)$ write $e_a=f_a^{-1}$ for the dual basis, and put $s_E=f_ae_a$. On overlaps $e_b=(f_a/f_b)e_a$, so $f_be_b=f_ae_a$: these sections glue. On $W=T\setminus E$ this section is nowhere zero and gives a specified trivialization $\tau_E:\mathcal O_W\simeq L_E|_W$. By [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor], $P_E=\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O_T,L_E)$ is a $\mathbf G_m$-torsor, with the specified section $\tau_E$ on $W$.

source.place: First sentence and final paragraph; canonical section on the complement

proof.text: Use [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] for $G=\mathbf G_m$ to obtain $\alpha_E=[(P_E,\tau_E)]\in H^1(T,W;\mathbf G_m)$. Its forgotten-support image is $[P_E]$. This is a specified class, not an arbitrary lift of a Picard class. Replacing $f_a$ by $u_af_a$ changes $e_a$ to $u_a^{-1}e_a$ and leaves $s_E$ unchanged. Thus the pair and its relative class are independent of all local equations.

source.place: First sentence: global well-definedness via a torsor with its specified section

proof.text: Put $m=\ell^n$, which is invertible on $T$ and kills $A$ in the conventions and coefficient prescription of [def-pur-frame-class]. Apply [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] and the relative connecting map of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] to form $\beta_E=\delta_{T,W}(\alpha_E)\in H^2(T,W;\mu_m^{\mathrm{et}})$. Its image in ordinary cohomology is $\delta_T([P_E])$, by the relative lemma's compatibility with forgetting support. Only the exact sequence of abelian sheaves is used here, with no tensoring of $\mathbf G_m$ over $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence; relative connecting construction from the blueprint final paragraph

proof.text: Identify relative cohomology with supported cohomology using [def-pur-support-cohomology], with the localization maps of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness]. Here is the resolution justification on both small sites. The localized site over the open object $W$ is the small site of $W$: an object is a morphism factoring through $W$, and forgetting that factorization and pulling back along the open immersion are inverse; the covering families are unchanged [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The slice restriction is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact] and preserves injectives by [new-over-pullback-preserves-injectives]. Thus, for an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$, the complexes $A^\bullet=I^\bullet(T)$ and $B^\bullet=I^\bullet(W)$ compute both derived global-section terms, with their restriction map $r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-injective-sheaf-mono-restriction], $r$ is degreewise surjective. The support complex is $K=\ker r$. Its inclusion $k\mapsto(k,0)$ into the signed relative complex $C^q=A^q\oplus B^{q-1}$, $D(a,b)=(da,r(a)-db)$, is a quasi-isomorphism: the quotient is $B^q\oplus B^{q-1}$ with differential $(x,y)\mapsto(dx,x-dy)$, contracted by $(x,y)\mapsto(y,0)$. The long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] then gives the assertion. This inclusion preserves the projection to $A$, hence forgetting support. Apply the canonical etale/pro-etale cohomology pullback [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison] to $T$ and $W$. The derived restriction square commutes because both maps restrict sections; its two vertical maps are quasi-isomorphisms, so the induced shifted-cone map is a quasi-isomorphism by the same long exact sequence. Apply next the roots coefficient morphism $\sigma_T\rho_T:\nu_T^{-1}\mu_m^{\mathrm{et}}\to A(1)_T$ of [def-pur-frame-class] and define $\operatorname{cl}(E)$ to be the image of $\beta_E$. These cone maps commute with projection to absolute sections, with restriction to etale neighbourhoods, and with inclusions of complements: the squares commute degreewise on sections and therefore on cones. This proves the needed forgetting, restriction and enlargement-of-support compatibilities, for every coefficient index $n\geq1$.

source.place: Support boundary and final paragraph; comparison performed on both terms of the relative cone

proof.text: Check the local formula, including both boundary signs. On a chart $U$ with $E_U=(f)$, the basis $e=f^{-1}$ trivializes $P_E$, and its specified section on $U_f$ has coordinate $f$. Use the resolution cone of [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology] for the canonical relative torsor class and connecting maps of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology], in the signed relative model $C^q=A^q\oplus B^{q-1}$ with $D(a,b)=(da,\operatorname{res}a-db)$. To check the torsor identification, use the canonical extension $0\to G\to E_P\to\mathbf Z\to0$ of [lem-sc-torsor-h1] and extend $G\to I^0$ to $E_P\to I^0$ by injectivity. Its differential factors through $\mathbf Z$ as a cocycle $a$; the chosen open section maps to $b$ with $db=\operatorname{res}a$. Changing the extension adds $(dx,\operatorname{res}x)$, a relative boundary. Conversely the fibre of $d:I^0\to I^1$ over $a$ is a $G$-torsor, with section $b$ on the complement. This computes the canonical relative class using the named absolute extension and its section. In particular the trivial torsor with section $f$ is represented by $(0,f)$, in additive notation for $\mathbf G_m$. In this model the localization boundary is $[b]\mapsto[(0,-b)]$: if $b$ lifts to $a$, adding $D(a,0)$ to $(0,-b)$ yields $(da,0)$, exactly the kernel-of-restriction connecting cocycle. Thus $\alpha_{E_U}=-\partial[f]$. Choose the degreewise split short exact sequence of injective resolutions for the Kummer sequence supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses]. On complement sections it remains degreewise split, so the augmented degree-zero cocycle $f$ in the right-hand resolution has a lift $r$ in the middle resolution. Its differential lies in the left-hand resolution and represents $\delta(f)$ under the usual connecting-map convention of [def-pur-frame-class]. Lifting $(0,f)$ to $(0,r)$ gives differential $(0,-dr)$, so $\delta_{U,U_f}(\alpha_{E_U})=[(0,-dr)]=\partial\delta(f)$. These computations are in resolutions or covering refinements, not an assumption that a fixed ordinary Cech cover computes all cohomology. After the coefficient map of step 5, this gives $\operatorname{cl}(E)|_U=\partial\kappa(f)$. For smooth $E=D$, this is exactly the single-factor frame class of [def-pur-frame-class]; [lem-pur-frame-independence] agrees with the independence already supplied by the global pair construction.

source.place: Clause (a), with explicit relative-cone boundary calculation

proof.text: For $E=D_1+D_2$ let $\mathcal I_E=\mathcal I_{D_1}\mathcal I_{D_2}$. On simultaneous Cartier charts $f_1f_2$ is a nonzerodivisor because both factors are, so $E$ is Cartier even when it is not smooth; its complement is $W=T\setminus(|D_1|\cup|D_2|)$. Multiplication identifies the ideal tensor product with the product ideal on these bases, hence $L_E\simeq L_{D_1}\otimes L_{D_2}$, carrying $s_E$ to $s_{D_1}\otimes s_{D_2}$. The frame torsor is therefore the contracted product by [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor], including its specified section over $W$. To see addition in relative $H^1$ from precisely the stated naturality of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology], take the product torsor for $\mathbf G_m\times\mathbf G_m$ and its pair of sections. The two projections give $(\alpha_{D_1},\alpha_{D_2})$ in relative cohomology, since the two-term restriction cone commutes with finite products. Push out along multiplication $\mathbf G_m\times\mathbf G_m\to\mathbf G_m$: on these additive cohomology groups it is addition, and on torsors it is their contracted product. Thus $\alpha_E=\alpha_{D_1}+\alpha_{D_2}$ in $H^1(T,W;\mathbf G_m)$. Here the two summands have first been restricted to the common complement, which is exactly enlargement of support. The connecting and coefficient maps of steps 4-5 are homomorphisms, so their images give the required equality in $H^2_Z(T,A(1))$. This proves global additivity without a local-to-global injectivity claim for $H^2_Z$.

source.place: Clause (b), addition; correcting the source two-function frame to the product equation

proof.text: Finally, step 4 gives $\operatorname{forget}(\beta_D)=\delta_T([P_D])$. Step 5 commutes with forgetting support, so $\operatorname{forget}(\operatorname{cl}(D))$ is the ordinary Kummer boundary of the frame-torsor class of $L_D=\mathcal O_T(D)$, followed by exactly the same roots coefficient morphism. This is $c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))$ by the definition in the statement. The torsor interpretation of the line bundle is [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor], and the compatibility of the relative connecting map with forgetting is the explicit last assertion of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology]. The equality holds globally; it is not deduced from restriction of ordinary $H^2$ to trivializing opens.

source.place: Final paragraph: forget-support comparison with the ordinary Kummer connecting class

proof_origin.place: Proof, with the relative torsor construction, explicit sign computation, and global rather than local comparison

split_report.summary: Constructed the supported divisor class globally from the Cartier line bundle with its specified section on the complement. Reused the existing relative torsor and Kummer interfaces; added one general smooth-pair coordinate lemma (Stacks 0FUE). Corrected the nonsmooth-sum domain, common support, product equation, arbitrary ramified coefficient index, and unsupported local-to-global inference for first Chern classes. The recovery review corrected the signed relative representative and made the source finite-type scheme convention explicit before invoking Noetherian permanence. Independent second reading supplied slice exactness/injectivity and an explicit contracted cone quotient, justified the torsor representative from its canonical extension, and cited split injective resolutions for the two boundary signs. The dry-run duplicate check exposed an existing exact dimension-drop lemma; the elementary Cartier corollary was removed from the new node and derived in step 1 using that existing node.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the first sentence (frames and well-defined class), clause (a) (local boundary), clause (b) (addition), and the final paragraph (forgetting support). The current main-20261015 text is unchanged in content but filed under sk-prop-an; the maintainer-owned unit binding is retained.

tool_uses.why: Generic equivalence between line bundles and units torsors, including tensor/contracted product; needed to form the relative pair and its sum, not a replacement of the unit computation.
Generic torsor-with-section classification and relative connecting maps supply a global lift and its compatibility; the unit provides no global relative Picard interface.
Exact Kummer sequence for schemes of arbitrary dimension; the unit computation uses this sequence too.
Generic comparison of the two small-site cohomologies on both terms of the restriction cone; no change of coefficient category is assumed.
Generic finite-type Noetherian permanence supplies the hypothesis of the smooth-pair Cartier corollary.
Generic injective restriction-surjectivity supplies the support kernel versus relative cone identification, not a purity theorem.
Generic slice restriction preserves injectives on either small site; needed to compute the two derived section terms by one resolution, and no purity-unit statement supplies this resolution fact.
Generic exactness of inverse image ensures the slice restriction remains a resolution on either site.
The named canonical torsor extension fixes the signs of the explicit local relative representative; it is a generic torsor tool, not a substitute for a purity step.
Generic split injective resolutions give actual lifts of the local Kummer cocycle; no unit-specific assertion supplies the horseshoe construction.

Exact generic Noetherian-local dimension-drop statement, reused successively in step 1 to deduce one equation from the source codimension convention; removes the elementary corollary from the new geometric node.

I confirm the STATEMENT-DISPUTED repairs. V(t)+V(t) on A^1 gives V(t^2), which is not smooth, so the source's sum lies outside its own domain. The frame (f1,f2) cuts out the intersection, not the sum. The P^1 argument for c1 fails: O(1) is trivial on both affines but c1 is nonzero. The repaired (b), stated for all Cartier divisors in H^2_{|D1|∪|D2|}, is a strengthening, not a weakening. The inline c1 matches the c1(O(1)) of def-amb-p1-trace, which the reviewed citer thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity uses. Steps: step 1 applies the dimension drop b times along the localized regular sequence (b=1 from the pure-codimension convention); I checked it, and it uses no regularity of B. In step 2 I checked the dual-basis transition by hand. In step 5 I checked the contraction of the cone quotient, and that r is surjective along an open monomorphism. In step 6 I recomputed the signs in the same model D(a,b)=(da,ra−db) used in the proof of lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology. The trivial torsor with section f is (0,f) and the localization boundary sends b to (0,−b), so the relative class is −∂[f]. The Kummer differential of the lift is (0,−dr), so the image is ∂δ(f) with a + sign, matching def-pur-frame-class. In step 7 the additivity follows from naturality under G_m×G_m projections and multiplication, and it is global. Step 8 is genuinely elementary. The new node lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates matches 0FUE together with the regular sequence from 067U in its proof. It holds on small cases (a point in A^1 gives b=1; Y=X gives b=0; Y empty is vacuous). It is not a restatement of a clause of the item. It is not a duplicate: I compared it with lem-sc-smooth-diagonal-regular-immersion, lem-pur-regular-immersion-linearization, sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form (054L), sk-lem-geometry, lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry and lem-pur-etale-at-point-from-differentials. Route: every off-route proof dependency is either a declared generic tool_use, which I accept, or a Mathlib leaf or definition. No coefficient categories are silently identified, there is no cycle, and no SGA source is used. The one fix: the new node lacked lean_audit.
